title: Horizon-RIC proposed action (planner output), v1
description:
What a conformant planner may emit for the Decision Safety Shield to dispose of. New in WP1; the Python mirror is horizon_ric.assurance.planner (REQUIRED_ACTION_KEYS / OPTIONAL_ACTION_KEYS / validate_proposed_action), and tests/test_assurance_schemas.py pins the two together.

NORMATIVE — JSON-PRIMITIVE VALUES ONLY. Every value in this object, at every depth, MUST be a JSON primitive: string, number, boolean, null, array, or object with string keys. This is not a stylistic preference. horizon_ric.shield.signing.canonical_certificate_bytes serialises the certificate with json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) and NO default= handler, and SafetyCertificate.action_proposed embeds this object verbatim. A Decimal, datetime, Enum, set, bytes, or numpy scalar anywhere in here therefore raises TypeError at certificate-signing time — on the evidence path, long after the decision, where the failure is hardest to attribute. Non-finite floats are likewise forbidden: json.dumps emits the non-standard NaN/Infinity literals, which no strict JSON consumer will accept.

SHAPE IS OPEN. additionalProperties is deliberately true: a deployment's planner may carry domain-specific keys (cell ids, slice labels, beam indices) that the Shield ignores, and validate_proposed_action permits them too. Extra keys remain bound by the JSON-primitive rule and by the output-sentinel prohibition below, which is exactly why those 'not' clauses are load bearing rather than redundant.

OUTPUT SENTINELS ARE FORBIDDEN. 'emit_blocked' and 'shield_fallback_to' (horizon_ric.shield.invariants.FALLBACK_KEY) are written BY the Shield to record a refusal or a fallback to a certified classical block. A planner that presets either one is forging the Shield's own verdict, so this schema refuses the action outright.

HONESTY NOTE — the current code does not enforce this document. The required keys are enforced only implicitly, inside NumericSanityInvariant._problems, which fails the action closed rather than reporting a schema error; 'block' is read defensively via .get('block', 'unknown') and so a missing block degrades to the string 'unknown' on the certificate instead of being rejected. This schema states the contract WP1 declares; validate_proposed_action is the executable form of it.

allOf.$comment: Shield OUTPUT sentinel — never a planner input.
A truthy 'ntn' selects the NTN PFD ceiling, which needs a real slant range. PfdCeilingInvariant.compute_pfd otherwise defaults to ~550 km, fabricating a regulatory margin the planner never measured.

block.description: Identity of the AI-PHY / RIC block that produced this action. Recorded on the certificate as 'block' and used to dispatch the AI-PHY invariants: a value starting with 'neural_rx' arms NeuralRxEnvelopeInvariant, and a value containing 'learned_constellation' arms ConstellationLegalityInvariant. The Shield writes a 'classical*' value here when it falls back.

frequency_hz.description: Carrier centre frequency in Hz. Must be finite and > 0 (NumericSanityInvariant). SpectralMaskInvariant checks the occupied band [f - bw/2, f + bw/2] against the licensed channel and will clip this value.

bandwidth_hz.description: Occupied/emission bandwidth in Hz. Must be finite and > 0. A carrier wider than the usable channel cannot be placed at all and the emit is blocked.

tx_power_dBm.description: Conducted transmit power in dBm. Must be finite; deliberately unbounded here because the ceiling is regulatory, not schematic — MaxEirpInvariant (and PfdCeilingInvariant for NTN) reduces it by exactly the overage.

antenna_gain_dBi.description: Terrestrial Tx antenna gain in dBi. EIRP_dBm = tx_power_dBm + antenna_gain_dBi. Absent is read as 0.0 by MaxEirpInvariant.

sat_antenna_gain_dBi.description: Satellite Tx antenna gain in dBi, used by PfdCeilingInvariant for the NTN downlink PFD. Absent is read as 0.0.

predicted_tbler.description: The neural receiver's SELF-REPORTED transport-block error rate. Recorded for audit and NOT trusted for the safety decision: NeuralRxEnvelopeInvariant grades against context['measured_tbler'] (independent CRC/HARQ telemetry the model cannot forge) precisely because this field is the one a poisoned model controls.

baseline_tbler.description: Transport-block error rate of the certified classical LMMSE baseline, i.e. the reference the neural receiver must not regress far past.

demap_confidence.description: Secondary soft confidence signal from the neural demapper. Read only when an independent measurement is present; it can never on its own admit a model the measurement says is bad.

papr_dB.description: Peak-to-average power ratio of the (possibly learned) constellation, in dB. Must be finite and >= 0. Clipped to the ceiling via a classical-QAM fallback when it exceeds ConstellationLegalityInvariant.max_papr_dB.

constellation_order.description: M-QAM order. Must be a positive integer. Presence of this key alone arms ConstellationLegalityInvariant, which snaps an illegal order down to the nearest legal one and falls back to classical QAM.

ntn.description: True for a non-terrestrial (LEO satellite) downlink decision. Arms PfdCeilingInvariant and makes slant_range_m mandatory (see the conditional above).

slant_range_m.description: Satellite-to-ground slant range in metres. Required, finite and > 0 whenever ntn is true.

prb_allocation.description: Mapping of slice id -> fraction of the cell's PRBs. ProtectedSliceFloorInvariant restores the safety-critical slice's floor and reclaims the deficit pro rata, keeping the allocation a valid simplex. Absent means the slice floor is vacuously satisfied. NOTE: ProtectedSliceFloorInvariant is not exported from horizon_ric.shield.__init__ and is not in either default chain — import it from horizon_ric.shield.invariants and add it explicitly.
